quote_text: Where you commence does not decide where you end. With self-belief and daily effort, even difficult beginnings can become the very thing that lifts you up. The world does not merely need spectators — it demands contributors, people who step in, add value, and make things better, one small step at a time. Continue. Persist. For at the meeting point of all your efforts, even those that seem unrelated, a synthesis shall emerge — coherent, strong, and undeniable. You shall not merely be remembered; you shall be sought. Become that person. Go beyond limits. Keep rising.

philosophy_text: My way of thinking rests on three main ideas: being skilled with technology, having the courage to create, and always choosing to do good. Building tools that solve real problems is not enough. You must also use those tools to help move society forward — especially in STEM education across Ghana and the rest of Africa. I do not build for short-term attention. I build for generational impact.
philosophy_revelation: For many years, I believed in staying quiet — thinking that excellent work would speak for itself. But I have come to see that silence, even with good intentions, can hide your light from the people who need to find you. Now I choose to share who I truly am, to declare my skills openly, and to invite others — partners, supporters, fellow builders — to work together. The world does not find what stays hidden. It seeks what is openly declared.

about_intro: I am a Ghanaian whose work spans multiple fields: technology, health sciences, writing, music, and public speaking. My professional identity does not fit a single category. Instead, I bring different competencies together with one commitment: building solutions that address real human needs while advancing STEM education across the African continent.
earlylife_desc: I attended Kwegyir Aggrey Memorial JHS (1999-2011), where I studied general science and learned about community service. It was during this period that I acquired basic computer skills — seeds that would later grow into my technology work. Between the ages of seventeen and nineteen, I served as a speaker in schools and at invited seminars, experiences that strengthened my ability to speak publicly and teach others.
secondary_desc: At Adisadel College (2011-2014), I pursued the General Science programme with Biology as my elective concentration. Beyond the curriculum, I assumed leadership as House Chaplain for Bishop LeMaire House and served as Scripture Union Music Director (2012-2014). Concurrently, I participated as a regimental bandsman throughout all three years — an experience that cultivated discipline and ensemble coordination. It was within the classrooms of Science 2 that the name Lemy Newman first emerged, as I quietly wrote musical compositions that would remain unseen by my peers until years later.
tertiary_desc: The University of Ghana (2016-2022) conferred upon me a Bachelor of Science in Botany, with specialization in Mycology within the Department of Plant and Environmental Biology. My time at Legon was marked by two commitments: academic rigor and leadership. I organized the Botany Society (2017-2018) and served as lead drummer at Believers' Loveworld Campus Ministry (2016-2019). The latter role introduced me to larger platforms, including participation in Night of Bliss with Pastor Chris and the Ministers' Conference with Reverend Benny Hinn, where I ministered as part of the choir and contributed as a protocol leader.
continuous_desc: I am committed to continuous learning. Alison provided international theoretical training culminating in Doula certification. Coursera has furnished credentials spanning web development, medical administration, and health sciences. The Pharmatrust Professional College awarded me Medicine Counter Assistant certification, duly recognized by the Pharmacy Council of Ghana. I have also received training in chiropractic wellness concepts through professional immersion at wellness centers in East Legon.

philosophy_intro: A short note on how I think, work, and move through the world — rooted in faith, driven by intention, and shaped by gratitude.
phil_belief_title: I believe in the power of intention.
phil_belief_body: What you focus on grows. I have learned to speak clearly about what I want, to move toward it with quiet discipline, and to stay open to the doors that open along the way. This is not superstition — it is attention.
phil_belief_quote: "As a man thinks in his heart, so is he." — Proverbs 23:7
phil_faith_body: Every skill I have, every door that has opened, every project that has shipped — I did not arrive here alone. I work hard, but I know who sustains the work. I give thanks where thanks is due.
phil_faith_quote: "Commit your work to the Lord, and your plans will be established." — Proverbs 16:3
phil_craft_body: I do not need to shout about what I do. The work speaks first. Every product shipped, every page written, every book published — that is the record. Consistency, over years, is louder than any announcement.
phil_people_body: The best technology is in service of people. A client who is understood, a student who finally gets it, a reader who feels seen — those moments matter more than any launch. I build with that in mind.
phil_growth_body: I am not the finished thing. Every project I ship teaches me something I did not know. I share what I learn, ask honest questions, and treat every collaborator as a teacher. Growth is a practice, not a badge.
philosophy_closing: These five things shape how I build, write, and work with people. Everything else follows.
